Roofing in Spring, TX

Spring has no city hall and no city roof inspector, and many of its houses are old enough that the deck under the shingles matters. One free call, any hour, reaches an independent, locally owned roofing company that answers Spring calls.

Call (832) 662-4107 What is under your shingles
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. Spring

A big community with no city limits

Roofing in Spring, TX works differently from roofing in a city, because Spring is not one. It is a census place and a mailing address that stretches across unincorporated Harris County and, north of Spring Creek, into Montgomery County.

The U.S. Census Bureau counted 62,559 people in the Spring census-designated place in 2020, up from 54,298 in 2010, and the Spring mailing address covers far more ground than that. The community started as a trading post William Pierpont set up on Spring Creek in 1838, according to the Texas State Historical Association. German farmers came in the 1840s, the Houston and Great Northern Railroad arrived in 1871, and by the early 1900s Spring had a roundhouse and a busy switchyard. When the rail jobs left, the old houses near the tracks were restored and turned into the shops of Old Town Spring.

Most of today's Spring was built much later, in subdivisions spreading out from FM 1960, Kuykendahl Road and Interstate 45. That spread is why the age and makeup of a Spring roof can vary so much from one street to the next.

Houston Expert Roofers is a phone line and a set of plain guides, nothing more. It owns no ladders and sends nobody to a roof. When a Spring homeowner calls, an automated voice assistant takes a short description of the trouble and the general location, then passes the call to an independent roofing company based in the Houston area. That company does the looking, the pricing, the work and the billing.

The deck question on older Spring houses

Neighborhoods such as Champion Forest, which Community Impact describes as about 1,469 single-family homes, and Memorial Northwest went up decades ago, many of their houses in the late 1970s and 1980s. On houses that age, the part of the roof nobody sees can change the price of a new one more than the shingles do.

What the code says

The International Residential Code treats wood shakes and asphalt shingles differently. Section R905.8 lets shakes go on spaced sheathing: rows of boards at least 1 by 4 inches, set apart to line up with the nails. Section R905.2.1 says asphalt shingles must be fastened to solidly sheathed decks. Shingles nailed over gaps have nothing to hold the nails and can sag between boards.

What that means on your house

If a house was first roofed with shakes, or if a later shingle roof was laid straight onto those boards, a proper replacement covers the whole roof in plywood or OSB before the underlayment goes down. That is a large line on a quote. A roofer can see which kind of deck you have from the attic in a few minutes, and it should show you photos before you sign.

Ask these before the tear-off

  • Did you look in the attic, and is my deck solid sheets or spaced boards?
  • Does the quote include new sheathing over the whole roof, or a per-sheet price for what you find?
  • Will you photograph the bare deck before it is covered, and send me the photos?
  • How many layers of old roofing are up there now, and does the price include removing all of them?

Two counties, almost no roof permits

Because Spring has no city government, nobody issues a Spring roofing permit and no city inspector climbs up after the job. What applies depends on which side of Spring Creek you live on.

Where the house isWhat the county saysWhat it means for you
North of Spring Creek, Montgomery CountyThe county's permitting FAQ says residential roof replacement does not require a permit; commercial roofs may need a fire code permit.No public inspection of the work. The contract and the roofer's photos are your record.
South of Spring Creek, unincorporated Harris CountyThe Office of the County Engineer requires permits for development in unincorporated areas, and its published permit types center on building, floodplain and septic work. It lists no separate re-roof permit.Ask the roofer whether your job needs anything from the county, and get the answer in writing. Structural changes are a different matter from a shingle swap.
Any Spring subdivision with deed restrictionsMany associations want plans and colors approved before work starts.Get approval first. Texas Property Code 202.011 limits an association's power to ban impact-resistant or energy-efficient shingles that look like allowed ones.

With no inspector in the picture, a written scope is the only thing holding the job to a standard. It should say full tear-off to the deck, name the underlayment, list new drip edge, pipe boots and flashing, give a per-sheet decking price, and promise photos at each stage.

Storms that hit Spring roofs

Spring is too far inland for storm surge, but recent years show how much damage wind alone does when pines and water oaks lean over nearly every lot.

DateWhat happened in and around Spring
May 16, 2024A derecho crossed the Houston area. ABC13 later described 60 to 80 mph gusts and two EF1 tornadoes in northwest Harris County neighborhoods.
July 8, 2024Hurricane Beryl. ABC13 reported trees still resting on houses in Spring's Timber Lane subdivision weeks later, and KHOU told of a Spring couple living in an RV after a 60-foot tree crushed their home. The Texas A&M Forest Service estimated that about half of the Houston area's trees took some hit.
November 24, 2025A tornado tore through Klein-area neighborhoods. The National Weather Service rated it EF-2, ABC13 reported about 100 homes damaged in northwest Harris County, and Associated Press coverage described torn roofs, garages shifted and smashed windows.

The quiet damage matters as much as the dramatic kind. A strong gust can break the seal strips on a row of shingles without tearing any off. From the street the roof looks fine, and the first sign is a stain on a bedroom ceiling a few rains later. If your roof went through 2024 and the 2025 tornado season without anyone looking at it, a look now is reasonable. Many roofers inspect at no charge; confirm that on the call.

Stay off the roof. Wet, storm-damaged roofs are slick and the decking may be weak, so leave the ladder in the garage. Keep well away from downed power lines and report them to your electric utility (CenterPoint Energy or Entergy Texas, whichever your bill names) or 911. Indoors, move belongings away from the leak, put a bucket or towels under the drip and keep people out of any room where the ceiling sags. Photograph the damage from the ground and inside the house, then call your insurer and a roofer.

Why Spring homeowners call the line

A quote that jumped for decking

The first roofer said shingles; the second said shingles plus a full new deck. Both may be honest, if one looked in the attic and one did not. Callers want a roofer that will check the boards and explain the difference with pictures.

A tree came through after the tornado or Beryl

A limb through the decking turns a roof job into a structural repair, with rafters, sheathing and the ceiling below. Spring callers with that kind of damage want a company that will close the opening against rain first and then rebuild the damaged section properly, with the structural work spelled out.

No inspector to catch mistakes

In a city, a permit inspection is a second set of eyes. On county land in Spring there is none. Homeowners who know that want a roofer that writes the full scope down and sends photos of the work at each stage.

An HOA approval to file first

Champion Forest, Memorial Northwest and many other Spring subdivisions carry deed restrictions. A roofer that knows the local associations can tell you what paperwork comes before the tear-off and which shingle colors usually get approved.

What a Spring re-roof usually involves

Most houses in Spring carry asphalt shingles, and most owners replace them with shingles again. The work itself is routine for any roofer. The decisions that change how long the new roof lasts are these:

  1. Deck first. Confirm solid sheathing, or price new sheathing, before choosing anything else.
  2. Pick the shingle for shade and wind. Lots under heavy canopy stay damp and grow dark algae streaks, so an algae-resistant shingle is worth asking about. Wind ratings differ between products; ask what the shingle is rated for and how it must be nailed to earn that rating.
  3. Fix the ventilation. Older Spring attics often have too little intake at the eaves. A hot, poorly vented attic shortens shingle life.
  4. Mind the trees. Ask which limbs over the roof should be trimmed before the new roof goes on, and who does that work.
  5. Register the warranty. Shingle makers' warranties often depend on registration and approved installation. Ask who registers it and get the paperwork.

For the money side, the roof replacement cost guide explains what moves a price, and the roof lifespan guide helps you judge whether yours has years left.

Questions to ask a roofer in Spring

About my house

  • Is my address in Harris County or Montgomery County, and does that change anything for this job?
  • Does my subdivision need to approve the roof first, and will you prepare the submission?
  • What did you see in the attic: decking type, ventilation, any rot?
  • Which overhanging limbs should come down before work starts?

About the company and the paperwork

  • Will your insurance agent send me a certificate of liability coverage?
  • Which roofs in Spring did you replace in the last year that I can drive by?
  • What does your workmanship warranty cover, for how long, and is it in the contract?
  • If this is an insurance job, what does your contract say about my deductible?

How a Spring call works

  1. Call the numberAn automated assistant answers (832) 662-4107 at any hour and asks which service you need, since the line also takes heating, cooling, pressure washing and water damage calls.
  2. Describe the roofA leak, missing shingles, hail, a limb on the roof or an old roof you want looked at, plus your part of greater Houston and how urgent it is.
  3. Get put throughYour call is transferred to an independent, locally owned roofing company, which hears a short summary before it picks up.
  4. Deal with the roofer directlyIt inspects, quotes and does the work, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it misses the call, it gets your name, number, city and need to call you back.

Texas has no state roofing license. No state agency licenses roofing contractors in Texas, and a 2025 bill to create one (HB 3344) did not reach a vote of the full House before the session ended. So check what you can: a certificate of liability insurance sent to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where your city requires one, local addresses you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration. Some cities also ask roofers to register. The line does not check any of this for you. How to check a roofer before you hire.

The deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance says it is illegal for a contractor to offer to waive, rebate or absorb your deductible, and a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice saying so. A roofer also may not act as your public adjuster on a property it works on. Treat any offer to "cover the deductible" as a reason to call someone else.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Who are the roofers in Spring, TX that this line connects me with?

Independent, locally owned roofing companies that take work in and around Spring. Houston Expert Roofers owns no trucks and employs no roofers. When you call, the line's automated assistant asks what kind of help you want, what the roof is doing and roughly where you are, then hands the call to one of those companies. It climbs up, writes its own price, does the job and collects its own payment from you. The call costs you nothing; companies may pay the line a fee for the introduction.

Is a permit required to put a new roof on in Spring, TX?

Spring is not a city, so there is no city roofing permit. North of Spring Creek the house sits in Montgomery County, whose permitting FAQ says residential roof replacement needs no county permit. South of the creek it is unincorporated Harris County, where the county engineer issues permits for development, mostly about floodplains; ask the roofer whether your job triggers one. Deed restrictions can still require approval first. See the county rules section.

Why would a roofer in Spring quote new plywood for the whole roof?

Because the deck under the shingles may be spaced boards rather than solid sheets. The residential code allows wood shakes on boards with gaps between them, but it says asphalt shingles must be fastened to a solidly sheathed deck. On an older house that once had shakes, or that had shingles laid over those boards, a sound shingle job means covering the roof in plywood or OSB first. Ask to see attic photos before you agree.

How do I find good roofing contractors in Spring, TX?

Texas licenses no roofers, so you build your own checklist. Ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the agent, a written contract that names the underlayment, flashing and decking price per sheet, and addresses of Spring roofs the company did that you can drive past. Compare at least two written quotes on the same scope. The roofer checking guide walks through each step.

Can I get help paying for Beryl roof damage in Spring?

It depends on which county your house is in. The Texas General Land Office opened 2024 disaster repair and reimbursement programs in July 2025 for 27 counties, Montgomery County among them, while residents of Harris County and the City of Houston were told to look to separate local programs funded by their own federal allocations. Income limits and primary-home rules apply, and funds are first come, first served, so check the GLO page to see whether applications are still open. The insurance claims guide covers the policy side.
